title: chrome.tabs.sendMessage without frameId reaches EVERY frame's content script — a shared record/session keyed by one recordId gets raced by iframes; gate handlers on window.top === window or target the originating frameId
trigger: a session/record dies instantly with a 'no-source'/'cancelled' error on multi-frame pages (YouTube embeds, ads iframes) even though the top frame has a perfectly good video
problem: On YouTube, CONDENSE_AUDIO_SESSION_START was delivered to every frame running the content script. The top frame started a healthy session and mounted the pill; an iframe with no <video> ran the same handler, hit the no-video branch, and posted failSession('no-source'). That error marked the SHARED record (one recordId) failed → background broadcast CONDENSE_AUDIO_EVENT 'failed' → the top frame tore down its own session → pill flashed and vanished, record ended 'cancelled' in <1s.
solution: Return early in the SESSION_START handler when window.top !== window — only the top frame owns the tab-scoped session. Additionally make the start path resilient: waitForVideoSource polls pickVideoElement up to SOURCE_WAIT_MS (8s) before failing 'no-source', so clicking record while metadata is still loading (duration 0) doesn't kill the session instantly.
principle: tabs.sendMessage is tab-scoped, not frame-scoped — every handler for a tab-scoped message that mutates shared background state must first decide which frame owns the action (top frame, or sender frameId from the originating content→bg message). If a failure branch in a non-owner frame can fail shared state, that's a race. Separately: 'no video found' at click time is often a timing artifact (metadata pending, SPA mount) — wait briefly before declaring no-source.
